content.question: How do Q-Learning and SARSA differ in terms of policy?
options: Q-Learning is on-policy, while SARSA is off-policy and evaluates actions chosen by a separate behavioral policy.
Both are off-policy, since each learns from transitions produced by an exploration policy rather than a fixed optimal one.
Q-Learning is off-policy, while SARSA is on-policy and learns the values of actions taken under its own current policy.
Both are on-policy; the difference lies only in the learning rate and the exploration schedule they apply.
content.answer: Q-Learning is off-policy, while SARSA is on-policy and learns the values of actions taken under its own current policy.
